summary: Function proxy round-trips causing intermittent E2E latency spikes and request timeouts
description: Issue summary: Since 2026-03-09 ~18:00 UTC Noteable Analytics (dedicated deployment in us-east) reports large increases in end-to-end request latency and intermittent request timeouts when tool/function calling is enabled. Impact: user-facing endpoints for document enrichment and extraction see tail latency spikes from ~200ms to 6–15s, and some requests hit the platform 30s request timeout. Preliminary hypothesis: schema validation and an extra validation/proxy round-trip introduced when tool calls are enabled is adding synchronous network hops under certain request paths, magnifying tail latency under bursty traffic. Environment: Dedicated pool, single model pinned redwood-v2-13b, API route /v1/generate with tool_call enabled and schema_validation=on. Reproducibility: intermittent; correlates with bursts and requests that include tool_metadata and complex tool schemas.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On a dedicated deployment with model pinned (redwood-v2-13b), enable tool_call and schema_validation flags for a route.
2) Send a mix of short and long prompts (100–800 tokens) that trigger a function/tool call (tool metadata schema attached).
3) Increase concurrency to 80–120 RPS to simulate production burst from the customer.
4) Observe end-to-end latency and streaming behavior; some requests time out at ~30s and streaming disconnects occur.
5) Toggle schema_validation to false and re-run the same load to compare latency distribution.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:24 - Support (Maya): Customer reports increase in 95th/99th latency after enabling tool calling; attached request ids and example payloads.

2026-03-10 10:05 - SRE (Ethan): Reproduced locally using dedicated test pool with similar schema; observed synchronous proxy request to schema-validator service adding 200–500ms per request and in some cases causing retry/backoff loops between proxy and validator.

2026-03-10 11:40 - Eng (Runtime): Function-proxy does an additional sync HTTP call to /validate-schema which calls into schema-validator (a separate service running on the control plane) before allowing the request through; under high concurrency, validator threadpool saturates and latency spikes propagate to E2E.

2026-03-10 12:10 - Observability: Dashboard shows validator CPU saturation in us-east region correlating with incidents; cache hit-rate for schema cache is low for dynamically generated tool schemas (customer constructed schemas per request).

2026-03-11 08:50 - Hypothesis: extra network hop + synchronous validation + lack of effective caching for dynamic schemas leads to tail amplification during bursts; streaming path exacerbates because proxy holds connection while waiting for validation, increasing chance of crossing API timeout threshold.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:30 - Maya (Support): Reached out to customer with request_ids and asked for a recent trace. Suggested temporary workaround: disable schema_validation flag or set tool_call to false for the most latency-sensitive routes.

2026-03-10 10:20 - Customer (Noteable Analytics, Dev lead - Priya Rao): Confirmed disabling schema validation reduced 99th latency from ~12s to ~400ms in our canary tests. Asked for a permanent fix; concerned about safety implications of turning off validation.

2026-03-10 12:25 - Ethan (SRE): Created dedicated investigation environment and simulated workload. Opened INT-445 to track control-plane validator capacity changes. Posting preliminary findings to #support and #sre.

2026-03-11 13:14 - Runtime Eng (Noah Li): Proposed two fixes: 1) move validation to async preflight for known schemas and respond with tokenized placeholder while validation is confirmed; 2) add a schema cache+TTL on the function-proxy to avoid repeated control-plane roundtrips for identical schemas. Draft PR references below.

2026-03-12 09:01 - Maya (Support): Customer accepted short-term workaround (disable validation) for their production routes while we schedule a fix. Customer requested timeline and risk assessment for change.
root_cause: Synchronous control-plane schema validation performed by function-proxy for every request that includes dynamic tool schemas. Under bursty traffic, schema-validator service threadpool and control-plane networking became saturated, adding 200–1200ms per request and causing occasional retries/timeouts which amplified tail latency.
resolution: Workarounds: 1) Customer disabled schema_validation for hot routes (verified reduction in tail latency). 2) Recommend increasing API request timeout to 60s for long-running jobs as a temporary mitigation. Permanent fix: Runtime team approved schema caching in function-proxy and an async validation flow for known schemas (PRs created). Plan: deploy schema-cache v1 to staging 2026-03-14 and to us-east prod canary 2026-03-16 followed by a full rollout.
next_steps: 1) Runtime Eng to merge caching PR and async validation PR and run performance tests (owner: Noah Li) - target merge date 2026-03-13.
2) SRE to add autoscaling knobs to schema-validator control-plane service and increase threadpool for us-east (owner: Ethan Brooks) - target 2026-03-14.
3) Support to coordinate a maintenance window for canary deploy with customer and monitor latency (owner: Maya Patel) - scheduled 2026-03-16 02:00-04:00 UTC.
4) Post-deployment, collect 7-day latency histogram and compare 99th percentiles vs baseline; if still elevated, escalate to product for architecture change.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-16 04:30 - Runtime: schema-cache v1 deployed to canary in us-east; initial telemetry shows 80% cache hit for Noteable's schemas and 95th latency reduced to 420ms.
2026-03-20 10:12 - SRE: Increased validator threadpool permanently for us-east and put autoscaling policy in place.
